items.cite: Howard Pollack, *George Gershwin: His Life and Work* (University of California Press, 2007).
items.note: A large documentary biography tracing how the songs, concert works and opera grew out of Gershwin’s working life, with separate chapters on the major scores and their reception.
A short study of Gershwin’s musical language in the Broadway theatre, published in Yale’s Broadway Masters series. Useful alongside the larger biography.

items.cite: Ira Gershwin, *Lyrics on Several Occasions* (1959; Limelight reprint, 2004).
items.note: Ira explains how he fitted words to tunes George had already composed, drawing on lyrics, discarded ideas and the circumstances of particular songs.

items.cite: Richard Crawford, ‘George Gershwin’s “I Got Rhythm” (1930)’, in *The American Musical Landscape: The Business of Musicianship from Billings to Gershwin* (University of California Press, 1993), chapter 7.
items.note: Crawford traces how one show tune became a jazz standard and the harmonic basis of other compositions, following performers and recordings as well as the Gershwins’ original song.
